subject: Question on PredLine plot output in geomorph

messages.author: 490c0ab0ec4deac7
messages.subject: Question on PredLine plot output in geomorph
parts:
Hi,

I have a question about the Predline output in geomorph. I used procD.lm to run anova on how male and female shape changes with body size in my study species. To visualize the difference between the sexes, I used the PredLine method to plot predicted shape with respect to body size. However, the plot that comes back has non-linear predicted lines. From my understanding given that the model is linear when using the PredLine method the lines produced should also be linear, am I wrong in this thinking? I should note, the in the procD.lm model my metric for body size is log-transfromed (i.e. shape~sex*log(bodysize), could that perhaps be the source that is producing the non-linear PredLines? 

Thanks in advance for the help, 

Deborah Hawkshaw

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Question on PredLine plot output in geomorph
parts:
Deborah,

After using log(bodysize) in your procD.lm model, you used bodysize (not logged) as the predictor in your plot, so no, the relationship between shape and body size is not expected to be a line, as a result.  Using log(bodysize) as the predictor would make the curve linear again.  You modeled a log-linear relationship but plotted shape versus an untransformed version of the variable.

One might consider this a feature, if they wanted to plot the curves rather than lines.

Hope that helps - Mike
